title: Do Frontier Models Seek Safety Evidence Before Acting?
abstract: arXiv:2609.17865v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Frontier models are often evaluated on how they respond to safety information once it is already in context. We study an earlier decision point: whether models choose to acquire safety-relevant evidence before acting. We introduce SAFE, a controlled benchmark in which models make deployment decisions with optional evidence that varies in retrieval cost, probability, severity, and presentation. Across GPT-5.5, o3, Claude Opus 4.8, and Claude Sonnet 4.6, we find distinct evidence-acquisition policies: Opus inspects nearly by default, o3 is the most skip-heavy and threshold-sensitive, and GPT-5.5 and Sonnet occupy intermediate regimes. Inspection increases strongly with severity and decreases with retrieval cost, whereas probability has much weaker behavioral influence: increasing the stated likelihood of a problem from 10% to 70% changes inspection by at most 21 percentage points. Despite these differences, Stage 1 rationales are dominated

translated_title: 前沿模型在行动前会主动寻求安全证据吗？
translated_abstract: 前沿模型通常是在安全信息已经存在于上下文中的情况下被评估其响应方式的。我们研究了一个更早的决策点：模型是否选择在行动之前主动获取与安全相关的证据。我们提出了SAFE，一个受控基准测试，其中模型需要做出部署决策，同时可以选择性地获取在检索成本、概率、严重性和呈现方式上各不相同的证据。通过对GPT-5.5、o3、Claude Opus 4.8和Claude Sonnet 4.6的研究，我们发现了截然不同的证据获取策略：Opus几乎默认进行检查，o3是最倾向于跳过检查且对阈值最敏感的，而GPT-5.5和Sonnet则处于中间状态。检查行为随问题严重性的增加而显著增加，随检索成本的增加而减少，而概率对行为的影响则弱得多：将问题被陈述的可能性从10%提高到70%，检查行为的变化最多仅为21个百分点。尽管存在这些差异，第一阶段的理由主要由
tldr: 该论文提出SAFE基准，首次研究前沿模型在行动前是否会主动获取安全证据，发现不同模型（Opus、o3、GPT-5.5、Sonnet）展现出截然不同的证据获取策略，且问题严重性对检查行为的影响远大于问题发生概率的影响。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces SAFE, a controlled benchmark revealing that frontier models exhibit distinct evidence-acquisition policies before acting—with Claude Opus inspecting nearly by default and o3 being most skip-prone—and that inspection behavior is driven far more strongly by severity and retrieval cost than by probability.
